written_before: any exceedance classifier was trained and before any sealed observation, label or reanalysis value was read
observed_before_amending: the validation-year (2012-2013) results of the regression grid: the selected regression arms improve RMSE and heavy-rain CSI over Raw there, but forecast very-heavy rain far too rarely (very-heavy frequency bias about 0.1) and do not exceed Raw's very-heavy CSI. No sealed-year value had been read.
problem: A conditional-mean regression cannot detect rare extreme cells: the categorical heavy and very-heavy questions of the problem statement are better asked of a probability model whose yes/no forecast uses a fixed probability threshold.
change: Adds exceedance arms to R05. For each arm B0 and B1 and each threshold (64.5 and 115.6 mm per 24 h) an XGBoost binary classifier P(rain >= threshold) is trained on 2000-2011 over an 8-configuration grid (depth 4 or 6, 200 or 350 rounds, positive-class weight none or the square root of the training imbalance, the fixed settings of the model specification otherwise). For every configuration the probability threshold tau is the quantile-grid value that maximises CSI on 2012-2013 subject to a frequency bias between 0.5 and 2.0 (heavy) or 3.0 (very heavy); the configuration with the highest validation CSI that is at least Raw's validation CSI is selected, ties to the earlier grid position, none qualifying means no candidate. The selected configuration is refit on 2000-2013 with tau unchanged. On the sealed years the categorical forecast is prob >= tau against the observed event; its CSI difference from Raw (raw >= threshold) is tested with the same paired whole-date bootstrap at 97.5 percent. A candidate bundle takes RMSE and bias from its regression arm and the heavy and very-heavy CSI from its exceedance classifiers; the tiers, BIAS_OK limits and support gate are unchanged. The regression-only comparison stays reported.
